---
title: "Quiz: A descriptive report"
---

[Exercises](15-descriptive-report.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/15-descriptive-report/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** Which input gives 24 complete plant growth values: `seedlings.csv` or
the repaired `seedlings-messy.csv`? What should a report state?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The repair exercise retains one unavailable final measurement.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
`seedlings.csv` has 24 complete growth values. The repaired messy input
has 24 plant records but 23 observed growths. State the input and report
available sample sizes consistent with it.
:::

---

**Q2.** A report says “Treated plants had a higher mean, so every treated plant
outgrew every control.” What should you inspect, and how would you revise it?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A group mean summarises observations without ordering every pair of plants.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Inspect the individual-point plot for overlap. Report the larger observed
mean with its units and sample sizes, while noting individual variation and
overlap between groups.
:::

---

**Q3.** What should the Methods and figure caption identify so a reader can
understand the growth summary?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
How were measurements obtained, and what does one point represent?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Identify the independent plant, treatment groups, initial/final readings
seven days apart, growth = final − initial in mm, input file, relevant data
checks, available n, and plotted symbol meanings. Label SD as individual spread.
:::

---

**Q4.** Your HTML renders only while objects remain in the RStudio Environment.
Which action tests and repairs this?

(i) Save a screenshot.  

(ii) Restart R and render, adding missing imports/calculations to the source.  

(iii) Rename the HTML.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The source should create every object needed by later chunks.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). A fresh-session render reveals hidden dependencies. Include loading,
import, checks, derived variables, summaries, and plots in the saved workflow.
:::

---

**Q5.** A report reads data from `/home/sam/Downloads/plants.csv`. Why might
a copied project fail? Give a more portable layout.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A personal absolute path points outside the copied project.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
That path may not exist elsewhere. Keep data inside the project, for
example `data/seedlings.csv`, and use that relative path from the report at
project root. Test the complete copy in a newly located folder.
:::
